# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `make docs` from the command definitions; edit internal/cli instead. -->

Every command reads `./gitopsify.yaml` when it exists (or `--config`); flags override it. Run `gitopsify <command> --help` for the same information in the terminal.

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`gitopsify adopt`](#gitopsify-adopt) | Prepare the target for takeover: back up and remove stale Helm release records |
| [`gitopsify bootstrap`](#gitopsify-bootstrap) | Install Argo CD or Flux in the target and point it at the generated repository |
| [`gitopsify check`](#gitopsify-check) | Preflight the target cluster: APIs, classes, existing owners, Helm records |
| [`gitopsify diff`](#gitopsify-diff) | Show what the first sync would change in the target cluster |
| [`gitopsify doctor`](#gitopsify-doctor) | Check that gitopsify can reach everything a migration needs |
| [`gitopsify generate`](#gitopsify-generate) | Write the GitOps repository |
| [`gitopsify init`](#gitopsify-init) | Describe a migration in gitopsify.yaml (interactive on a terminal) |
| [`gitopsify migrate`](#gitopsify-migrate) | Generate, push, check and bootstrap in one go |
| [`gitopsify rules`](#gitopsify-rules) | List the built-in exclusion rules |
| [`gitopsify scan`](#gitopsify-scan) | Inventory the source cluster: what would be migrated, how, and what is left out |
| [`gitopsify skills`](#gitopsify-skills) | Install the gitopsify skills for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot) |
| [`gitopsify skills install`](#gitopsify-skills-install) | Copy the skills to where your AI coding agents find them |
| [`gitopsify skills list`](#gitopsify-skills-list) | List the bundled skills |
| [`gitopsify skills show`](#gitopsify-skills-show) | Print a skill's SKILL.md |
| [`gitopsify status`](#gitopsify-status) | Show whether Argo CD or Flux has synced every app of an environment |
| [`gitopsify version`](#gitopsify-version) | Print the version |
| `gitopsify completion bash\|zsh\|fish\|powershell` | Shell completion scripts |

## gitopsify adopt

Prepare the target for takeover: back up and remove stale Helm release records.

```text
When Argo CD (which renders charts itself) or plain manifests take over objects
installed with Helm, the release records left in the cluster go stale and a
later "helm upgrade" would fight the GitOps tool. adopt backs them up and, with
--helm-records backup-delete, removes them. Flux HelmReleases reuse the records,
so they are kept.

Pair it with "generate --adopt", which writes takeover-safe sync settings.
```

Usage: `gitopsify adopt [flags]`

```sh
  gitopsify adopt --env prod --helm-records backup-delete
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--backup-dir` | `.gitopsify-backup/helm-records` | where backups are written |
| `--dry-run` |  | show what would happen |
| `--helm-records` | `backup` | keep, backup or backup-delete |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  | don't ask for confirmation |

**Scope**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--cluster-scoped` |  | cluster-scoped objects: auto, all or none |
| `--disable-rule` |  | disable a built-in exclusion rule (see "gitopsify rules"; "*" for all) |
| `--exclude-app` |  | drop these apps (globs) after grouping |
| `--exclude-kind` |  | never migrate these kinds |
| `--exclude-namespace` |  | skip these namespaces (globs, repeatable) |
| `--from-file` |  | read the source objects from YAML/JSON files or directories instead of a cluster, e.g. kubectl get -A -o yaml output ("-" for stdin; repeatable) |
| `--include-managed` |  | also migrate objects already managed by Argo CD or Flux |
| `--kind` |  | migrate only these kinds (Deployment, ingress.networking.k8s.io, svc...) |
| `-n`, `--namespace` |  | migrate only these namespaces (globs, repeatable) |
| `--no-deps` |  | with --resource/--selector, don't pull in dependencies |
| `-r`, `--resource` |  | migrate specific objects, plus what they need: kind[.group]/[namespace/]name or helm/namespace/release (repeatable) |
| `-l`, `--selector` |  | migrate objects matching this label selector, plus what they need |

**Helm**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--artifacthub` |  | look up unknown chart repositories on Artifact Hub |
| `--helm-mode` |  | Helm releases: auto, chart, vendor or manifests |
| `--helm-repo` |  | repository of a chart: chart=https://... or chart=oci://... (repeatable) |

**Cleaning, grouping and ordering**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--clean` |  | cleaning strategy: auto, managed-fields, heuristic or minimal |
| `--depends-on` |  | make an app depend on others: app=dep1,dep2 (repeatable) |
| `--group-by` |  | split objects into apps by namespace, label or single |
| `--group-label` |  | label used with --group-by label (default app.kubernetes.io/part-of) |
| `--no-order` |  | don't order apps (no sync waves or dependsOn) |
| `--wave` |  | pin an app (glob) to a wave: app=N (repeatable) |

**Environment transforms**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--image-registry` |  | rewrite image prefixes: from=to, e.g. test.azurecr.io=uat.azurecr.io (repeatable) |
| `--ingress-class` |  | map IngressClasses: from=to (repeatable) |
| `--namespace-map` |  | rename namespaces: from=to (repeatable) |
| `--replace` |  | replace a string everywhere, also in Helm values: from=to (repeatable) |
| `--storage-class` |  | map StorageClasses: from=to (repeatable) |

**Target cluster access**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--env` |  | environment to act on: name or name=kube-context (default: the first one) |
| `--target-as` |  | impersonate this user on the target cluster |
| `--target-as-group` |  | impersonate this group on the target cluster (repeatable) |
| `--target-as-uid` |  | impersonate this UID on the target cluster |
| `--target-certificate-authority` |  | CA file (PEM) the target cluster's API server certificate is checked against |
| `--target-client-certificate` |  | client certificate file (PEM) for the target cluster |
| `--target-client-key` |  | client key file (PEM) for the target cluster |
| `--target-context` |  | kubeconfig context of the target cluster (default: the current context) |
| `--target-in-cluster` |  | use the ServiceAccount of the pod gitopsify runs in for the target cluster |
| `--target-insecure-skip-tls-verify` |  | don't verify the target cluster's API server certificate (test clusters only) |
| `--target-kubeconfig` |  | kubeconfig of the target cluster (several files separated like in KUBECONFIG) |
| `--target-proxy-url` |  | http(s) or socks5 proxy for the target cluster's API server |
| `--target-request-timeout` |  | timeout of each API request to the target cluster, e.g. 30s |
| `--target-server` |  | API server URL of the target cluster, overriding the kubeconfig's |
| `--target-tls-server-name` |  | server name to verify the target cluster's API server certificate against |
| `--target-token` |  | bearer token for the target cluster (or $GITOPSIFY_TARGET_TOKEN); never written to files |
| `--target-token-file` |  | file with a bearer token for the target cluster |


## gitopsify bootstrap

Install Argo CD or Flux in the target and point it at the generated repository.

```text
Installs the pinned Argo CD or Flux release in an environment's cluster, applies
the settings the generated apps rely on, registers the repository credentials and
applies the root object (argocd/<env>/root.yaml or clusters/<env>/flux-system).
Push the generated repository first. Doesn't need the source cluster.
```

Usage: `gitopsify bootstrap [flags]`

```sh
  gitopsify bootstrap --env uat --git-token "$GITHUB_TOKEN"
  gitopsify bootstrap --env uat --ssh-key ~/.ssh/deploy --known-hosts known_hosts
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `-o`, `--output` |  | directory of the generated repository (default from the configuration) |

**Bootstrap**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--git-token` |  | password or token for an HTTPS repository (or GITOPSIFY_GIT_TOKEN) |
| `--git-username` |  | username for an HTTPS repository (default git) |
| `--known-hosts` |  | known_hosts file of the Git server, e.g. from ssh-keyscan (needed by Flux over SSH, and by Argo CD for hosts other than GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps) |
| `--sops-age-key` |  | age key file loaded as Flux's SOPS decryption key |
| `--ssh-key` |  | private key file for an SSH repository |
| `--timeout` | `15m0s` | how long to wait for Argo CD or Flux to start (image pulls are the slow part) |
| `--wait` |  | after bootstrapping, wait until every app is synced and healthy |
| `--wait-for` | `healthy` | what --wait waits for: healthy, or synced (applied, health aside) |
| `--wait-timeout` | `20m0s` | how long --wait waits |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  | don't ask for confirmation |

**Target cluster access**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--env` |  | environment to act on: name or name=kube-context (default: the first one) |
| `--target-as` |  | impersonate this user on the target cluster |
| `--target-as-group` |  | impersonate this group on the target cluster (repeatable) |
| `--target-as-uid` |  | impersonate this UID on the target cluster |
| `--target-certificate-authority` |  | CA file (PEM) the target cluster's API server certificate is checked against |
| `--target-client-certificate` |  | client certificate file (PEM) for the target cluster |
| `--target-client-key` |  | client key file (PEM) for the target cluster |
| `--target-context` |  | kubeconfig context of the target cluster (default: the current context) |
| `--target-in-cluster` |  | use the ServiceAccount of the pod gitopsify runs in for the target cluster |
| `--target-insecure-skip-tls-verify` |  | don't verify the target cluster's API server certificate (test clusters only) |
| `--target-kubeconfig` |  | kubeconfig of the target cluster (several files separated like in KUBECONFIG) |
| `--target-proxy-url` |  | http(s) or socks5 proxy for the target cluster's API server |
| `--target-request-timeout` |  | timeout of each API request to the target cluster, e.g. 30s |
| `--target-server` |  | API server URL of the target cluster, overriding the kubeconfig's |
| `--target-tls-server-name` |  | server name to verify the target cluster's API server certificate against |
| `--target-token` |  | bearer token for the target cluster (or $GITOPSIFY_TARGET_TOKEN); never written to files |
| `--target-token-file` |  | file with a bearer token for the target cluster |


## gitopsify check

Preflight the target cluster: APIs, classes, existing owners, Helm records.

```text
Checks an environment's cluster against what would be deployed to it:
  - every kind and API version is served (or its CRD is migrated)
  - referenced StorageClasses and IngressClasses exist
  - objects that already exist, and which tool owns them now
  - Helm release records that would go stale
  - controllers needed by SealedSecrets/ExternalSecrets
Exits with status 1 when a check fails.
```

Usage: `gitopsify check [flags]`

```sh
  gitopsify check --env uat
  gitopsify check --env uat=kind-uat --format json
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--format` | `table` | output format: table, json or yaml |

**Scope**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--cluster-scoped` |  | cluster-scoped objects: auto, all or none |

| `--exclude-app` |  | drop these apps (globs) after grouping |
| `--exclude-kind` |  | never migrate these kinds |
| `--exclude-namespace` |  | skip these namespaces (globs, repeatable) |
| `--from-file` |  | read the source objects from YAML/JSON files or directories instead of a cluster, e.g. kubectl get -A -o yaml output ("-" for stdin; repeatable) |
| `--include-managed` |  | also migrate objects already managed by Argo CD or Flux |
| `--kind` |  | migrate only these kinds (Deployment, ingress.networking.k8s.io, svc...) |
| `-n`, `--namespace` |  | migrate only these namespaces (globs, repeatable) |
| `--no-deps` |  | with --resource/--selector, don't pull in dependencies |
| `-r`, `--resource` |  | migrate specific objects, plus what they need: kind[.group]/[namespace/]name or helm/namespace/release (repeatable) |
| `-l`, `--selector` |  | migrate objects matching this label selector, plus what they need |

**Environment transforms**

**Secrets**

## gitopsify diff

Show what the first sync would change in the target cluster.

```text
Server-side dry-runs every generated object against an environment's cluster
(as a new field manager, like Argo CD and Flux) and compares the result with the
live object. Use it before a takeover: a clean diff means the first sync is a
no-op. Helm apps are rendered with helm template when helm is installed.
```

Usage: `gitopsify diff [flags]`

```sh
  gitopsify diff --env prod
  gitopsify diff --env prod --exit-code   # fail CI on changes
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--exit-code` |  | exit with status 2 when the sync would change anything |
| `--format` | `table` | output format: table, json or yaml |
| `--no-helm-template` |  | compare Helm apps using their recorded release manifests |
| `--show-unchanged` |  | also list unchanged objects |

**Scope**

| Flag | Default | |

## gitopsify doctor

Check that gitopsify can reach everything a migration needs.

```text
Checks, without changing anything:
  - the configuration file
  - the tools gitopsify calls: git, helm, kubectl or kustomize, sops
  - the source cluster: connection, how you authenticate, who you are and
    whether you may read everything
  - each environment's cluster: the same, and whether you may install Argo CD
    or Flux there (cluster-admin), and the sealed-secrets controller
  - the Git repositories: whether they can be reached with your credentials
Exits with status 1 when a check fails.
```

Usage: `gitopsify doctor [flags]`

```sh
  gitopsify doctor
  gitopsify doctor --env uat --target-kubeconfig ~/.kube/uat.yaml
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--format` | `table` | output format: table, json or yaml |

| `--cluster-scoped` |  | cluster-scoped objects: auto, all or none |

| `--exclude-app` |  | drop these apps (globs) after grouping |
| `--exclude-kind` |  | never migrate these kinds |
| `--exclude-namespace` |  | skip these namespaces (globs, repeatable) |
| `--from-file` |  | read the source objects from YAML/JSON files or directories instead of a cluster, e.g. kubectl get -A -o yaml output ("-" for stdin; repeatable) |

## gitopsify generate

Write the GitOps repository.

```text
Runs the whole pipeline against the source cluster and writes the repository.

Maturity levels:
  --tool none     clean Kustomize apps and Helm values; wire them up yourself
  --tool argocd   plus Applications/ApplicationSets, an AppProject and a pinned
                  Argo CD bootstrap (--pattern app-of-apps|applicationset|single)
  --tool flux     plus Flux Kustomizations, HelmReleases and a pinned Flux bootstrap

Re-running it updates the files it generated and keeps files you added.
```

Usage: `gitopsify generate [flags]`

```sh
  # test was built by hand; generate an Argo CD app-of-apps repo for uat
  gitopsify generate --context test --tool argocd --env uat=uat-cluster \
    --repo-url https://github.com/acme/platform-gitops.git

  # Flux, one repository per environment, sealed Secrets
  gitopsify generate --tool flux --layout repo-per-env --env uat --env prod \
    --secrets sealed-secrets --repo-url git@github.com:acme/gitops.git

  # just one app and what it needs, as plain manifests
  gitopsify generate -r deployment/shop/web -o ./web

  # Argo CD takes over the cluster it was exported from
  gitopsify generate --tool argocd --adopt --env prod=prod --repo-url ...
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` |  | list the files that would be written |
| `-i`, `--interactive` |  | choose the apps to migrate interactively |

**Scope**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--cluster-scoped` |  | cluster-scoped objects: auto, all or none |
| `--disable-rule` |  | disable a built-in exclusion rule (see "gitopsify rules"; "*" for all) |
| `--exclude-app` |  | drop these apps (globs) after grouping |
| `--exclude-kind` |  | never migrate these kinds |
| `--exclude-namespace` |  | skip these namespaces (globs, repeatable) |
| `--from-file` |  | read the source objects from YAML/JSON files or directories instead of a cluster, e.g. kubectl get -A -o yaml output ("-" for stdin; repeatable) |
| `--include-managed` |  | also migrate objects already managed by Argo CD or Flux |
| `--kind` |  | migrate only these kinds (Deployment, ingress.networking.k8s.io, svc...) |
| `-n`, `--namespace` |  | migrate only these namespaces (globs, repeatable) |
| `--no-deps` |  | with --resource/--selector, don't pull in dependencies |
| `-r`, `--resource` |  | migrate specific objects, plus what they need: kind[.group]/[namespace/]name or helm/namespace/release (repeatable) |
| `-l`, `--selector` |  | migrate objects matching this label selector, plus what they need |

**Helm**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--artifacthub` |  | look up unknown chart repositories on Artifact Hub |
| `--helm-mode` |  | Helm releases: auto, chart, vendor or manifests |
| `--helm-repo` |  | repository of a chart: chart=https://... or chart=oci://... (repeatable) |

**Cleaning, grouping and ordering**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--clean` |  | cleaning strategy: auto, managed-fields, heuristic or minimal |
| `--depends-on` |  | make an app depend on others: app=dep1,dep2 (repeatable) |
| `--group-by` |  | split objects into apps by namespace, label or single |
| `--group-label` |  | label used with --group-by label (default app.kubernetes.io/part-of) |
| `--no-order` |  | don't order apps (no sync waves or dependsOn) |
| `--wave` |  | pin an app (glob) to a wave: app=N (repeatable) |

**Environment transforms**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--image-registry` |  | rewrite image prefixes: from=to, e.g. test.azurecr.io=uat.azurecr.io (repeatable) |
| `--ingress-class` |  | map IngressClasses: from=to (repeatable) |
| `--namespace-map` |  | rename namespaces: from=to (repeatable) |
| `--replace` |  | replace a string everywhere, also in Helm values: from=to (repeatable) |
| `--storage-class` |  | map StorageClasses: from=to (repeatable) |

reads gitopsify.yaml from the current directory.

## gitopsify migrate

Generate, push, check and bootstrap in one go.

```text
Runs the whole migration for one environment:
  1. scan the source cluster and write the repository (generate)
  2. commit, and push with --push
  3. preflight the target cluster (check); stops on failures
  4. install Argo CD or Flux and apply the root object (bootstrap)
It asks before changing the target unless --yes is given.
```

Usage: `gitopsify migrate [flags]`

```sh
  gitopsify migrate --context test --env uat=uat --tool argocd \
    --repo-url https://github.com/acme/gitops.git --push --git-token "$TOKEN"
```

| `--no-order` |  | don't order apps (no sync waves or dependsOn) |
| `--wave` |  | pin an app (glob) to a wave: app=N (repeatable) |

**Environment transforms**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--image-registry` |  | rewrite image prefixes: from=to, e.g. test.azurecr.io=uat.azurecr.io (repeatable) |
| `--ingress-class` |  | map IngressClasses: from=to (repeatable) |
| `--namespace-map` |  | rename namespaces: from=to (repeatable) |
| `--replace` |  | replace a string everywhere, also in Helm values: from=to (repeatable) |
| `--storage-class` |  | map StorageClasses: from=to (repeatable) |


## gitopsify skills

Install the gitopsify skills for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot).

```text
gitopsify ships agent skills: playbooks an AI coding agent follows to run a
migration with you, including the parts gitopsify leaves to people on purpose -
creating the remote repository on GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps or Bitbucket,
deploy keys, installing controllers, loading Secrets into a secret manager and
verifying the result.

The skills use the open Agent Skills format. Claude Code users can also install
them as a plugin (/plugin marketplace add hayone1/gitopsify), and Gemini CLI
users as an extension (gemini extensions install https://github.com/hayone1/gitopsify).
```


## gitopsify skills install

Copy the skills to where your AI coding agents find them.

```text
Copies every gitopsify skill into the skills directory of the chosen agents,
replacing earlier versions of the gitopsify skills and leaving other skills
alone. By default they go to your home directory for the agents most people
use: ~/.agents/skills (Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) and
~/.claude/skills (Claude Code). --project installs into the current project
instead, to share them through Git.

Agents: agents (also codex, opencode, antigravity), claude, copilot, cursor,
gemini, or all.
```

Usage: `gitopsify skills install [flags]`

```sh
  gitopsify skills install
  gitopsify skills install --agent claude --project
  gitopsify skills install --dir ~/my-agent/skills
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent` |  | agents to install for: agents, claude, copilot, cursor, gemini, codex, opencode, antigravity or all (default agents,claude) |
| `--dir` |  | install into this skills directory instead |
| `--dry-run` |  | print where the skills would go |
| `--project` |  | install into the current project instead of your home directory |


## gitopsify skills list

List the bundled skills.

Usage: `gitopsify skills list [flags]`


## gitopsify skills show

Print a skill's SKILL.md.

Usage: `gitopsify skills show <skill> [flags]`


## gitopsify status

Show whether Argo CD or Flux has synced every app of an environment.

```text
Reads the Argo CD Applications, or the Flux Kustomizations and HelmReleases, that
gitopsify generated for an environment and reports their sync and health. Objects
the generated repository declares but the cluster doesn't have yet are reported as
Missing. Doesn't need the source cluster.

Exits with status 1 when something isn't ready (or, with --wait, isn't ready in
time).
```

Usage: `gitopsify status [flags]`

```sh
  gitopsify status --env uat
  gitopsify status --env uat --wait --timeout 15m   # in CI, after bootstrap
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--format` | `table` | output format: table, json or yaml |
| `-o`, `--output` |  | directory of the generated repository (default from the configuration) |
| `--timeout` | `15m0s` | how long --wait waits |
| `--wait` |  | wait until everything is synced and healthy |
| `--wait-for` | `healthy` | what --wait waits for: healthy, or synced (Argo CD applied everything, health aside) |

**Target cluster access**

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--env` |  | environment to act on: name or name=kube-context (default: the first one) |
| `--target-as` |  | impersonate this user on the target cluster |
| `--target-as-group` |  | impersonate this group on the target cluster (repeatable) |
| `--target-as-uid` |  | impersonate this UID on the target cluster |
| `--target-certificate-authority` |  | CA file (PEM) the target cluster's API server certificate is checked against |
| `--target-client-certificate` |  | client certificate file (PEM) for the target cluster |
| `--target-client-key` |  | client key file (PEM) for the target cluster |
| `--target-context` |  | kubeconfig context of the target cluster (default: the current context) |
| `--target-in-cluster` |  | use the ServiceAccount of the pod gitopsify runs in for the target cluster |
| `--target-insecure-skip-tls-verify` |  | don't verify the target cluster's API server certificate (test clusters only) |
| `--target-kubeconfig` |  | kubeconfig of the target cluster (several files separated like in KUBECONFIG) |
| `--target-proxy-url` |  | http(s) or socks5 proxy for the target cluster's API server |
| `--target-request-timeout` |  | timeout of each API request to the target cluster, e.g. 30s |
| `--target-server` |  | API server URL of the target cluster, overriding the kubeconfig's |
| `--target-tls-server-name` |  | server name to verify the target cluster's API server certificate against |
| `--target-token` |  | bearer token for the target cluster (or $GITOPSIFY_TARGET_TOKEN); never written to files |
| `--target-token-file` |  | file with a bearer token for the target cluster |


## gitopsify version

Print the version.

Usage: `gitopsify version [flags]`


## Global flags

Every command accepts these.

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `-c`, `--config` |  | configuration file (default ./gitopsify.yaml when it exists) |
| `--no-color` |  | disable colors (also honors NO_COLOR) |
| `--no-input` |  | never prompt; fail instead where a prompt would be needed |
| `-q`, `--quiet` |  | only print results and errors |

**Source cluster access** (see [authentication](authentication.md))

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--as` |  | impersonate this user on the source cluster |
| `--as-group` |  | impersonate this group on the source cluster (repeatable) |
| `--as-uid` |  | impersonate this UID on the source cluster |
| `--certificate-authority` |  | CA file (PEM) the source cluster's API server certificate is checked against |
| `--client-certificate` |  | client certificate file (PEM) for the source cluster |
| `--client-key` |  | client key file (PEM) for the source cluster |
| `--context` |  | kubeconfig context of the source cluster (default: the current context) |
| `--in-cluster` |  | use the ServiceAccount of the pod gitopsify runs in for the source cluster |
| `--insecure-skip-tls-verify` |  | don't verify the source cluster's API server certificate (test clusters only) |
| `--kubeconfig` |  | kubeconfig of the source cluster (several files separated like in KUBECONFIG) |
| `--proxy-url` |  | http(s) or socks5 proxy for the source cluster's API server |
| `--request-timeout` |  | timeout of each API request to the source cluster, e.g. 30s |
| `--server` |  | API server URL of the source cluster, overriding the kubeconfig's |
| `--tls-server-name` |  | server name to verify the source cluster's API server certificate against |
| `--token` |  | bearer token for the source cluster (or $GITOPSIFY_TOKEN); never written to files |
| `--token-file` |  | file with a bearer token for the source cluster |
